title: Minimum Time to Eat All Grains
statement:
Hens and grains sit at integer points of a number line: hen `i` starts at `hens[i]` and grain `j` lies at `grains[j]`. Positions may repeat.

Every second, each hen may move one unit to the left, move one unit to the right, or stay where it is; all hens move at the same time and independently of one another. A hen eats a grain instantly whenever both are at the same point, and one hen may eat any number of grains.

Return the minimum number of seconds needed for every grain to be eaten when the hens move optimally.
notes:
## Intuition

If the hens can finish in `t` seconds, they can also finish in any longer time, so the answer can be found by **binary search on `t`**. Trying every assignment of grains to hens would be exponential; instead we only need a fast yes/no test for one `t`.

For that test, sort both arrays and sweep from the left. The leftmost uneaten grain must be eaten by somebody; if it lies to the left of the current hen, every later hen is even farther away, so this hen must take it. A hen that walks `back` units left and then right (or right first and then back) covers the furthest right point when it picks the better order:

- left first: it ends at `hen + (time - 2 * back)`;
- right first: it can go `floor((time - back) / 2)` to the right and still get back to the grain in time.

## Approach

1. Sort `hens` and `grains`.
2. `canFinish(time)`: keep `next`, the first uneaten grain. For each hen, if that grain is to its left at distance `back > time`, fail. Otherwise compute `reach`, the furthest point to the right it can also visit, and skip every grain up to `reach`.
3. The test passes when all grains were skipped.
4. Binary search `time` between `low = 0` and `high` = the time for the first hen to walk to the leftmost grain and then sweep to the rightmost one, which always works.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted: `hens = [3, 6, 7]`, `grains = [2, 4, 7, 9]`. For `time = 1`: hen 3 eats grain 2 (`back = 1`, `reach = 3`); hen 6 faces grain 4 with `back = 2 > 1`, so it fails. For `time = 2`: hen 3 eats 2; hen 6 has `back = 2`, `reach = 6`, eats 4; hen 7 has `reach = 9` and eats 7 and 9. The search settles on `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O((n + m) log(n + m) + (n + m) log R): sorting, then about 31 checks of one linear sweep each (R is the answer's range, up to about 2·10^9).
- Space: O(1) besides the sort.

## Pitfalls

- When the hen also needs to go left, take the **better** of the two orders; using only "left first" overestimates the time.
- Sort **both** arrays: the greedy step relies on the leftmost uneaten grain being the current hen's job, which is only true in sorted order.
- Do not compute `high` as a fixed small number: the answer can exceed 10^9 (for example, grains on both far sides of one hen).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `canFinish` | whether every grain can be eaten within `time` seconds |
| `next` | index of the leftmost grain not yet eaten |
| `hen` | position of the current hen in sorted order |
| `back` | how far left of `hen` the grain `grains[next]` is |
| `reach` | the rightmost point this hen can also visit |
| `low`, `high`, `mid` | the binary search window over the answer |

narration.2: Sort the hens so they can be handled from left to right.
narration.3: Sort the grains so the leftmost uneaten grain is always grains[next].
narration.4: canFinish answers: can all grains be eaten within time seconds?
narration.6: Give each hen, from left to right, the leftmost grains still uneaten.
narration.7: Every grain is already eaten, so the remaining hens are not needed.
narration.8: If the hen only goes right, it reaches hen + time.
narration.9: The leftmost uneaten grain is to the left of this hen, so this hen must eat it.
narration.11: Too far to the left even with all the time; no later hen is closer, so time is too short.
narration.12: Pick the better order: left then right, or right then back to the left grain.
narration.14: Every grain up to reach is eaten by this hen on the way.
narration.16: Success only if no grain is left.
narration.19: Walking to the leftmost grain and sweeping right always works, so it bounds the answer.
narration.20: Shrink the window until a single time remains.
narration.22: If mid is enough time, the answer is mid or smaller.
narration.25: Otherwise the answer is larger than mid.
narration.28: low is the smallest time that passes the test.
